title: The Perfect Alibi
premise: True-crime podcaster Theo Thackeray has spent three years documenting the 1987 disappearance of heiress Vivian Marsh, the coldest case in the records of Hollow Creek. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to the crime, one promising 'more if you find her'—Theo discovers the confession is forged and that a witness everyone believes dead, court stenographer Ada Lune, may have faked her death to escape the town's most powerful family. As Theo follows Ada's trail through sealed probate files and a corrupted inheritance scheme, she realizes the Marsh fortune was built on a second, unrecorded victim. In the end Theo finds Ada alive in hiding, exposes the surviving conspirator—Vivian's own brother, now the town's beloved judge—and broadcasts the truth, though at the cost of the archive she spent years perfecting.
about_author: Wendell Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town court reporter who spent a decade transcribing depositions before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about archives, secrets, and the people who keep both.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. In her basement archive of the Marsh case, Theo records episode forty-one, cataloging the town's polite evasions with clinical detachment. A knock at the door delivers two envelopes: one signed confession to Vivian Marsh's murder, one unsigned note reading 'She isn't where they buried her.' The beat: curiosity cracking open long-buried obsession.

chapters.title: The Confession That Lies
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. The confessed man, dying ex-deputy Roy Pell, recants within hours of Theo's visit—he can't describe the house he claims he burned down. Comparing handwriting against old court transcripts, Theo spots a match to someone else entirely: Ada Lune, the stenographer who vanished in 1990, presumed drowned. The beat: the thrill of a thread pulled loose.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. Townsfolk repeat the same polished story of Ada's drowning, too identical to be honest. At the flooded quarry, Theo finds a memorial stone newer than the death date it commemorates. Judge Edmund Marsh, Vivian's brother, warns her off gently, kindly, and with unmistakable weight. The beat: first real fear beneath the excitement.

chapters.title: What the Transcript Omitted
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. Digging into sealed probate records, Theo learns Vivian's will named an unknown beneficiary—a trust administered by Judge Marsh that quietly absorbed the estate after her death. A redaction in the inquest transcript sits exactly where Ada's testimony would have been. The beat: the cold realization that the corruption is structural, not incidental.

chapters.title: The Second Victim
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Theo and Ada (in letters). Interleaved with Theo's search are pages from Ada's hidden journal, mailed in installments: there were two bodies that night in 1987, and only one made the record. Ada saw who signed the silence into existence. The beat: dread deepening as the case doubles in size.

chapters.title: A House That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. Breaking into the shuttered Marsh estate, Theo finds Ada's old steno machine and a practice ribbon typed with names—not witnesses, but payees. Someone has been living in the east wing; the dust tells a story of recent habitation. Headlights sweep the drive. The beat: hunted, heart pounding, closer than ever.

chapters.title: The Judge's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. Judge Marsh invites Theo to tea, offering funding for her podcast and a subtle threat wrapped in nostalgia: he knows about her mother's debts, her sister's custody trouble. He offers her the archive's legitimacy in exchange for the letters. The beat: power showing its smiling face, and Theo understanding what it costs to refuse.

chapters.title: Where the Dead Go to Wait
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. Following the journal's final clue—a ferry ticket never used—to a coastal nursing home under a false name, Theo comes face to face with Ada Lune, old, sharp, and furious at being found. Ada agrees to talk on one condition: everything goes out live, unedited, tonight. The beat: the witness found, the clock now audible.

chapters.title: Live Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. From the nursing home, Theo streams episode forty-two: Ada's testimony naming Judge Marsh as the architect of both deaths and the forged confession meant to close the case forever. Listeners flood in; the county sheriff, listening en route, arrives not to stop them but to arrest him. The beat: cathartic climax—the archive turned weapon.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Record
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. Weeks later, Marsh awaits trial and Ada testifies in daylight. Theo burns her alphabetized filing system and begins a new archive organized around living voices instead of dead facts. The last letter's promise—'more'—arrives once more, empty except for a single word: 'Thank you.' The beat: resolution, grief transmuted into purpose.
